{"answer":"Problem description:
Calculate the percentage (integer) of the available system memory that is currently used on an Ubuntu Linux system. The program/script you supply must print only a single integer (no text, no trailing characters, no decimals). The calculation should use the kernel-reported "available" memory value (not "free"), so: used = total - available, percent = (used * 100) / total, output as an integer (floor/truncate).

Initialization script (init.sh) — deploys the example script into the student's home directory:
#!/bin/bash
mkdir -p "$HOME/mem_monitor"
cat > "$HOME/mem_monitor/calc_mem_usage.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
free -b | awk '/^Mem:/ {printf "%d\n", ($2 - $7) * 100 / $2}'
EOF
chmod +x "$HOME/mem_monitor/calc_mem_usage.sh"
# optional: print path of installed script
printf "%s\n" "$HOME/mem_monitor/calc_mem_usage.sh"

Example calculation script (calc_mem_usage.sh) — prints only an integer:
#!/bin/bash
free -b | awk '/^Mem:/ {printf "%d\n", ($2 - $7) * 100 / $2}'

Usage:
1) Run the initializer to deploy the script:
   bash init.sh
2) Run the example script to get a single integer (percentage):
   ~/mem_monitor/calc_mem_usage.sh

Notes:
- Uses "free -b" so the calculation is done in bytes (avoids rounding from human units).
- awk printf "%d" truncates to an integer (floor behavior for positive numbers).
- Output of the example script is exactly one integer and a newline."}
